admission.justification: Ownership is settled at preparation, reused by publication, rebuilt by the saved-target check, and reclaimed by the report-collection routes; no one of those places can keep one request's alias honest across its whole life.

applicability: Every request that publishes a hand-over locator, across start, repeat, restart, resume, saved-launch restore and terminal report collection.
conditions: A repeat of the exact request reuses the alias; a lost alias is rebuilt at the report folder its receipt records; a name that would lead to another folder is refused before any hand-over file is written.
The alias stays available, or is deterministically rebuilt, for as long as the seat can resume.
Terminal report collection removes only the alias, never the report folder, and only when it leads into the folders being reclaimed.
exclusions: Report-folder collection, fsync, atomic replacement and failure preservation, which the report-collection contract carries.
A locator that leads outside the reclaimed folders, which is left standing and reported.
statement: A request reuses its locator, restores a deleted locator before validating frozen details, refuses collision or retarget before sending, and removes aliases only through terminal report collection.
